sentences.en: This episode today, as so many of my favorite episodes are,
sentences.zh: 今天的这期节目，就像我许多最喜欢的节目一样，

sentences.en: I was actually suggested by a listener, a listener called Josephine, who sent me this message.
sentences.zh: 其实是由一位听众建议的，一位名叫约瑟芬（Josephine）的听众给我发了这条消息。

sentences.en: And she's given me permission to read it out loud and see if any of you may relate.
sentences.zh: 她同意让我大声读出来，看看你们当中是否有人也有同感。

sentences.en: This is what she had to say.
sentences.zh: 她是这样说的：

sentences.en: Hi, Gemma.
sentences.zh: 嗨，杰玛。

sentences.en: It's been a while since I felt any kind of emotion and I'm not trying to sound dramatic.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没有感受到任何情绪了，我这么说绝不是在夸大其词。

sentences.en: I mean, truly.
sentences.zh: 我是说真的。

sentences.en: Happiness, sadness, excitement.
sentences.zh: 快乐、悲伤、兴奋。

sentences.en: They've all disappeared.
sentences.zh: 它们全都消失了。

sentences.en: My childhood dog recently died and I felt nothing.
sentences.zh: 我从小陪伴到大的狗狗最近去世了，但我毫无感觉。

sentences.en: I got a big promotion that I wanted for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我得到了心仪很久的大好晋升。

sentences.en: Also nothing.
sentences.zh: 同样毫无波澜。

sentences.en: One emotion I am feeling is fear.
sentences.zh: 我唯一能感受到的情绪是恐惧。

sentences.en: Fear that I'll never feel the same way again.
sentences.zh: 我害怕自己再也无法找回以前的感受了。

sentences.en: I can link it back to some really bad anxiety I had almost a year ago.
sentences.zh: 这可以追溯到大约一年前我经历过的一次非常严重的焦虑。

sentences.en: Around that time, I started to intellectualize almost all of my emotions before I allowed myself to fully feel them.
sentences.zh: 大约从那时起，我在允许自己真正去感受之前，几乎把所有的情绪都理性化了。

sentences.en: And now I feel like I've ruined my brain by cutting off its pathway to expression permanently.
sentences.zh: 现在我觉得自己彻底毁了大脑，永远切断了它表达情感的通路。

sentences.en: Please, any advice I need and would love for you to do an episode on how to actually feel my feelings.
sentences.zh: 求求你，我需要任何建议，非常希望能做一期节目来聊聊如何才能真正去感受自己的情绪。

sentences.en: So I got this message and firstly, thank you, Josephine, for sharing.
sentences.zh: 所以我收到了这条消息，首先，谢谢约瑟芬的分享。

sentences.en: But I got this message and I immediately knew I needed to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 但我收到这条消息时，我立刻就知道我必须谈谈这个话题。

sentences.en: In fact, I actually had a whole other episode planned for this week.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我这周原本计划了另一期完整的节目。

sentences.en: But this one just felt so much more like important because Josephine, like me too, I am here with you.
sentences.zh: 但这一期感觉要重要得多，因为约瑟芬，我也一样，我就在这里陪着你。

sentences.en: I'm experiencing the same kind of emotional blunting and the same kind of poor communication between me and my emotions.
sentences.zh: 我也正在经历同款的情感迟钝，以及我和自己情绪之间同样糟糕的沟通。

sentences.en: You know, I feel happiness and I confuse it as something bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我感受到快乐，却把它当成什么不好的事。

sentences.en: I feel sadness, grief, anger, stress.
sentences.zh: 我感受到悲伤、悲痛、愤怒、压力。

sentences.en: I push it down and say, I'll get to that later.
sentences.zh: 我把它压下去，告诉自己以后再说。

sentences.en: I also, much like you, intellectualize my emotions as a way of getting out of feeling them.
sentences.zh: 我也和你很像，把情绪理性化作为逃避感受它们的一种方式。

sentences.en: You know, overanalyzing every possible cause, explanation and consequence until I'm exhausted.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，过度分析每一个可能的起因、解释和后果，直到自己筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: And you know what, I don't feel particularly good about it and I don't feel like it's a particularly great way to live.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道吗，对此我并没有感觉特别好，我也觉得这并不是一种特别棒的生活方式。

sentences.en: The absence of any negative emotions doesn't necessarily make your life a happy one because your emotions all use the same systeMs.
sentences.zh: 没有任何负面情绪并不一定会让你的生活变得幸福，因为你的所有情绪都在使用同一套系统。

sentences.en: All 34,000 distinct emotions we can feel are operating across the same neural pathways, across all the same cortexes of the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们能感受到的所有34000种不同情绪，都是通过相同的神经通路、大脑的相同皮层在运作。

sentences.en: And that's why nostalgia and regret feel so similar.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么怀旧和遗憾感觉如此相似。

sentences.en: Passion and anger, trust and vulnerability, anxiety and excitement, grief and gratitude.
sentences.zh: 激情与愤怒、信任与脆弱、焦虑与兴奋、悲伤与感激。

sentences.en: They feel very similar.
sentences.zh: 它们感觉非常相似。

sentences.en: So you turn off one, you turn off regret, you turn off anger, vulnerability, anxiety, grief.
sentences.zh: 所以你关闭其中一个，你就关闭了遗憾，关闭了愤怒、脆弱、焦虑、悲伤。

sentences.en: You also turn off nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 你也关闭了怀旧。

sentences.en: You also turn off passion, trust, excitement, gratitude.
sentences.zh: 你也关闭了激情、信任、兴奋、感激。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of us are finding ourselves in that very position where we've tried to feel, we've tried to manage our negative emotions in a way that's actually meant
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都发现自己正处于这种境地：我们曾试图去感受，曾试图以某种方式管理我们的负面情绪，而这种方式实际上意味着

sentences.en: we've prevented any intense emotion at all.
sentences.zh: 我们阻止了任何强烈情绪的产生。

sentences.en: I think a reason for that is that we're scared not of our actual emotions, we're scared of our feelings about our feelings.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中的一个原因在于，我们害怕的不是我们真实的情绪，我们害怕的是我们对于情绪的情绪。

sentences.en: Like, let me explain this.
sentences.zh: 这么说吧，让我解释一下。

sentences.en: I know it sounds like a little bit strange, but you know, if I feel sad,
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来有点奇怪，但你知道的，如果我感到悲伤，

sentences.en: I feel like that's a bad thing and I feel like it's the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一件坏事，而且感觉就像世界末日一样。

sentences.en: If I'm angry, I worry that something is wrong with me.
sentences.zh: 如果我生气，我就会担心自己出了什么问题。

sentences.en: So it's not that the sadness is bad.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是悲伤本身不好。

sentences.en: It's not that the, you know, the grief or the anger is bad.
sentences.zh: 并不是，你知道的，悲痛或愤怒本身不好。

sentences.en: It's that I believe that it's going to make me feel miserable or have some further on consequence.
sentences.zh: 而是我相信它会让我感到痛苦，或者带来某些后续的后果。

sentences.en: This whole experience, this whole pattern, this is known as metacognition or meta-emotions.
sentences.zh: 整个经历、整个模式，被称为元认知或元情绪。

sentences.en: My emotions, our emotions, about the possibility of certain emotions.
sentences.zh: 我们对可能产生的特定情绪所抱有的情绪。

sentences.en: And if that sounds complicated to you, it most certainly is.
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来很复杂，它确实非常复杂。

sentences.en: And it's complicated for our brain and it's difficult for us to work through that and feel like we can actually feel our feelings.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的大脑来说很复杂，对我们而言也很难去理清并感觉自己真正能去感受情绪。

sentences.en: So the two big questions we're really left with is why?
sentences.zh: 所以我们真正面临的两个核心问题是：为什么？

sentences.en: You know, why does this happen?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: And how, how do I fix it?
sentences.zh: 以及如何做，我该如何解决它？

sentences.en: How do I convince myself
sentences.zh: 我该如何说服自己

sentences.en: I'm not at the mercy of my emotions and actually let them back in and feel human and feel connected again?
sentences.zh: 我没有任由情绪摆布，而是真正让它们重新进来，去感受做人的滋味，重新建立连接？

sentences.en: Well, my lovely listeners, we are going to discuss exactly that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我可爱的听众们，我们接下来就要讨论这个。

sentences.en: We are going to explore the psychology behind all of this and so much more.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨这一切背后的心理学以及更多内容。

sentences.en: Be prepared to go deep, maybe shed a few tears because today I really want us to all leave feeling in touch with at least one emotion we've been suppressing.
sentences.zh: 准备好深入探讨吧，或许还会掉几滴眼泪，因为今天我真的希望我们所有人离开时，都能重新连结上哪怕一种我们一直在压抑的情绪。

sentences.en: Just one.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一种。

sentences.en: That's all we want at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们归根结底所追求的。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，我们这就开始吧。

sentences.en: So we need to talk about this firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得先谈谈这个。

sentences.en: We need to talk about what being detached from our emotions actually looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们得谈谈与情绪脱节究竟是什么样子的。

sentences.en: I was literally, I was about to say, what does it feel like?
sentences.zh: 我刚才差点就要说，这感觉是什么样的？

sentences.en: But, you know, that's the actual problem we're dealing with.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这正是我们正在处理的实际问题所在。

sentences.en: What does it look like?
sentences.zh: 它看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: Not being able to feel your feelings essentially means you've put up some kind of wall between you and the actual feeling.
sentences.zh: 无法感受你的情绪，本质上意味着你在自己和真实感受之间筑起了一道墙。

sentences.en: So it's not necessarily the absence of any emotion at all.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不一定意味着完全没有任何情绪。

sentences.en: You are not broken.
sentences.zh: 你并没有坏掉。

sentences.en: The emotions are still there.
sentences.zh: 情绪依然在那里。

sentences.en: It's just that when an emotion comes up, you might feel it for just a second.
sentences.zh: 只是当情绪涌现时，你可能只会感受到短短的一秒钟。

sentences.en: Perhaps you notice it and then you start overanalyzing or you get freaked out that it's going to come out too large and too loud.
sentences.zh: 也许你注意到了它，然后你开始过度分析，或者你被它可能会变得过于汹涌和剧烈吓坏了。

sentences.en: So you distract yourself or minimise or adopt any number of coping strategies.
sentences.zh: 于是你转移注意力、将其淡化，或者采取各种应对策略。

sentences.en: After long enough, you can no longer name what the sensation or emotion even is.
sentences.zh: 时间久了，你甚至再也说不出那种感觉或情绪究竟是什么了。

sentences.en: And in some extreme cases, you might also take direct action to completely avoid the trigger.
sentences.zh: 在某些极端情况下，你甚至可能会采取直接行动来彻底避开导火索。

sentences.en: You know, if someone has hurt you or broken your heart, you would perhaps consider and tell yourself, well, they don't even exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果有人伤害了你或伤了你的心，你可能会考虑并告诉自己，好吧，这个人根本就不存在了。

sentences.en: And I'm never going to think about them again.
sentences.zh: 我再也不会去想他们了。

sentences.en: Meaning that a lot of the, you know, deep grief or betrayal or the emotions that you should be working through because of that experience remain unhealed, remain untouched.
sentences.zh: 这意味着许多由于这段经历而本该去处理的深刻悲痛、背叛感或各种情绪，依然没有痊愈，依然无人触及。

sentences.en: Maybe you're really struggling because you've got like a terrible grade on a uni assignment and you're such a perfectionist and this is just like the most awful thing.
sentences.zh: 也许你正备受煎熬，因为你在大学作业里拿了个糟糕的分数，而你又是个完美主义者，这简直就像是最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: You might try and manage that and not feel the feeling by completely disengaging with your studies or together or completely ignoring any upcoming assignments
sentences.zh: 你可能会试着应付过去，通过彻底退出学业或者完全忽略接下来的所有作业来逃避这种感受

sentences.en: because you don't even want to give the illusion of trying.
sentences.zh: 因为你甚至不想给人一种你在努力的假象。

sentences.en: So this is known as avoidance and it's often a precursor to not feeling your feelings, not even putting yourself in the search, in the circumstances or the situations
sentences.zh: 这被称为回避，它通常是无法感受情绪的前兆，甚至不会让自己置身于可能产生这种感受的环境、条件或情境之中。

sentences.en: in which that might even be possible.
sentences.zh: 所以当觉得与自己的感觉脱节时，当你经历麻木、也许还有延迟的情绪反应（即糟糕的事情发生了，你并没有真正去想它，

sentences.en: So when you feel out of touch with your feelings, when you're experiencing numbness, maybe a delayed emotional response, so something bad happens, you don't really think about it
sentences.zh: 直到一个月后），当你回避充满情感的情境，当你经历冷漠，

sentences.en: until a month down the line, when you are avoiding emotional situations, when you're experiencing apathy,
sentences.zh: 当你，你知道的，觉得自己虽然可能有一段时间没感到悲伤了，但也一直没感到快乐，这种情况有一个词。

sentences.en: when, you know, you feel like, yes, you may not have been sad for a while but you also haven't been happy, there is a word for this.
sentences.zh: 它被称为情感迟钝，或者在医学上称为情感表达减少（reduced affect display）。

sentences.en: It's called emotional blunting or in medicine, reduced effect display.
sentences.zh: 我听过对情感迟钝真正含义的最佳描述，其实来自于一个参与该经历案例研究的患者，

sentences.en: The best description I've heard of that describes what emotional blunting really is, it actually came from a patient involved in a case study on this experience
sentences.zh: 这位患者正在经历强烈的情感麻木和迟钝，她说，这经常让我感觉自己像个隐形人，觉得自己像个幽灵，

sentences.en: and this patient was experiencing intense emotional numbing and blunting and she said, often what this makes me feel like is I feel invisible, I feel like I'm a ghost,
sentences.zh: 我看着我的家人彼此互动，但有一道无形的屏障阻挡着我加入他们。

sentences.en: I watch my family engaging with each other but there is an invisible barrier that keeps me from joining them.
